title: The brighter the light, the deeper the shadows

context_sources.name: International Dark Sky Association
context_sources.role: Lighting regulations cited for the social strategy

limitations: The notation table and several equations lost their symbols in extraction.
The projection pursuit step function prints in a broken form.
The cell-to-grade mapping names cell VI under two grades.
The summary and the body disagree on Jintang's improvement, 11.1 against 17.81 percent.
The robustness-band thresholds in Table 7 are unreadable.
Page 23, the leaflet, has no text layer and was read from the page image.

tasks: Build a light pollution risk assessment model
Grade four location types in China and explain the grades
Design three intervention strategies and measure their effect
Pick the best strategy for two locations and publish a leaflet

section_map.summary: Grades B, C, A, A, then a social win for Chengdu and an economic win for Jintang.
The 1930s origin, three categories, and a rejection of a blind ban.
Five tasks ending in a leaflet.
One unit per region, no government cost, and independent indicators.
Damage and requirement scores from projection pursuit, graded on a GE matrix.
Chengdu B, Jintang C, the village and the reserve A.
A goal program with priority factors and soft constraints.
Six orderings scored by distance to the ideal corner.
The city rises to grade A and the suburb to grade B.
Errors of 1.5 and 3.0 percent inside the flat part of each curve.
A Chengdu flyer headlined by the lost starry sky and a 30 percent cut.

contributions.summary: Harm and need are scored separately, so a place is not punished for needing light.
The weights are estimated once on forty countries and reused everywhere.
Priority factors let one program express three different strategies.
The winning strategy is the one closest to a stated ideal corner.

dependency_graph.handoff: The two scores and the projection weights become the plan's targets and coefficients.
Each solved priority order supplies the scores whose distance to the corner is measured.
The winning plan is the one whose parameters are swept.

assumptions.summary: A region is one unit, so internal differences are ignored.
Government cost is left out of the strategies.
The secondary indicators are mutually independent.
Weights fitted on forty countries apply to every site.
Closer to the corner (0, 1) is always a better outcome.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Indicators are min-max normalized before weighting.
Forty countries provide the sample for projection pursuit.
Population density, light intensity, and lighting counts for the four Sichuan sites.
The appendix lists both scores for all forty countries.

models.summary: Grades a site from damage and requirement scores on a nine-cell matrix.
Sets indicator targets with a goal program ranked by priority factors.
Picks the priority order closest to the ideal corner.
Grades the plan by its worst percentage error under parameter sweeps.

verification.summary: Each grade is checked against what the place is known for.
The chosen parameters sit past the inflection point of each curve.
The mean absolute percentage error is 1.5 percent for Chengdu and 3.0 percent for Jintang.

results_trace.summary: Chengdu grade B, Jintang grade C, Xingfu Village and Baishuihe grade A.
The social strategy wins in Chengdu and the economic strategy in Jintang.
Chengdu's grade rises from B to A after intervention.
Jintang's damage score falls from 0.726 to 0.554 and its grade rises from C to B.

writing_logic.summary: Open on a proverb, then name the models, then the grades.
Concede the benefit of light before listing its harm.
Follow every assumption with a justification.
State the two perspectives before splitting the indicators.
Explain the borrowed tool by the analogy that makes it fit.
Translate each constraint into a plain rule of thumb.
Write the search as numbered pseudocode.
Support each admitted weakness with an example.

language_observations.summary: The title states the tradeoff as a proverb.
The benefit is granted in full before the harm is raised.
The imported matrix is given both its names.
A site that scores well is still given a reason for concern.
The flyer repeats the model's own 30 percent figure.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: A judge rewards scoring the benefit of light separately from its harm.
A judge rewards a strategy that changes with the type of place.
A judge penalizes a grade mapping that assigns one cell to two grades.

weaknesses.summary: The notation symbols were lost in extraction.
The projection pursuit formulas print with missing symbols.
Cell VI is listed under both grade A and grade C.
The constraint caps differ between sites with no stated rule.
Jintang's improvement is 11.1 percent in the summary and 17.81 percent in the body.
The indicator set is limited by the lack of a data standard.

independent_extensions.statement: Add the cost of the lamps and the enforcement to the goal program and re-rank the six orderings.
independent_extensions.reason: The paper itself says the missing cost could reverse the recommended strategy.

independent_extensions.statement: Resolve the grade mapping so each of the nine cells belongs to exactly one grade, and recompute the four results.
independent_extensions.reason: The printed mapping names one cell twice, so the grades are not reproducible.

candidate_rule_impacts.impact: Supports checking a plan by sweeping its parameters and grading the result with a forecast error.
Supports choosing the intervention by the priority order that lands closest to a stated ideal point.

unresolved_questions: Which of the two reported improvements for Jintang, 11.1 or 17.81 percent, is correct.
How the constraint caps were chosen for each site.
What thresholds separate the four robustness bands.
